title: The balance sheet
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers the balance sheet or the accounting equation; the nearest, financing a new business, explains equity and debt but not how assets, liabilities and owner's equity are reported together.

draft.title: The balance sheet
card: A balance sheet is a financial statement that shows what a business owns and owes at one point in time, such as 30 June. It is a snapshot, not a record of a period.
something the business owns that has value, such as cash, stock, equipment or property.
an amount the business owes to others, such as a bank loan or money owed to suppliers.
the owner's share of the business. It is what is left after liabilities are taken from assets, so assets = liabilities + owner's equity.
draft.remember: A balance sheet is a snapshot of what a business owns and owes on one date.

a.q: Which of these best describes what a balance sheet shows?
opts: The assets, liabilities and equity on one date
The revenue and expenses earned over a year
The cash received and paid out over a month
The planned income and spending for next year
a.why: A balance sheet is a snapshot of assets, liabilities and owner's equity on one date. A statement of revenue and expenses over a period is an income statement, which is the most tempting wrong option because it also covers the business's finances.
a.clue: Think of a photo taken on one day, not a film.

b.q: On 30 June, Priya's bakery in Orange has assets of $90,000 and liabilities of $35,000. What is her owner's equity?
b.why: Owner's equity = assets minus liabilities, so $90,000 - $35,000 = $55,000. Adding the two gives $125,000, which mixes up the formula: liabilities are taken away from assets, not added to them.
b.clue: Equity is what is left after the debts are taken from assets.

a.best: The assets, liabilities and equity on one date
